correctness.rationale: Over Q the projective Jacobian equations force all nonzero coordinates to share the same p-th power; normalization reduces them to the p-th roots of unity, and divisibility by the cyclotomic minimal polynomial enforces balanced counts. In the x_N=1 chart, elimination of x_(N-1) gives Hessian determinant -[p(p+1)]^(N-2) times the product of nonzero coordinate inverses, proving every candidate is an ordinary double point and the Jacobian singular scheme is reduced. The resulting zero-dimensional singular support proves geometric integrality and normality for N>=5. All roots occur, so ratios generate Q(zeta_p) and all residue fields have degree p-1. S_N orbit stabilizers are S_m^p semidirect C_p or AGL_1(F_p) as appropriate. Exact independent small cases (3,2) and (5,1) agree, without replacing infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prime-order cyclotomic cancellation is a known input (Lam--Leung, arXiv:math/9511209, theorem 2.2); it is not claimed as novel. Searches and relevant full-text comparisons did not identify the complete characteristic-zero projective nodal singular scheme, its exact Q(zeta_p) residue fields for every odd prime, or the S_N/AGL(1,p) closed-point structure. Cafure--Matera--Privitelli study a distinct finite-field code-derived symmetric hypersurface family; Catanese--Tonoli address even sets of nodes on sextic surfaces. A latent corollary or unindexed source remains a risk.

value.rationale: The family is defined by the canonical all-ones hyperplane section of a Fermat hypersurface, and prime cyclotomy enforces a sharp dimension-independent smooth/nodal boundary. Exact finite-etale singular schemes, complete residue-field splitting, and symmetric/Galois orbit structures are natural and nonredundant invariants for arithmetic nodal geometry and descent. The output is a general structural classification, not a merely arbitrary isolated calculation; no higher topology or positive-characteristic classification is claimed.
